meta.scope: Park-wide rules, climate, tides, SAR/incident patterns, and current road/facility conditions for Olympic National Park.
meta.status: COMPLETE first pass (2026-10-07). See uncertain items flagged with confidence low/medium or stale:true.
meta.confidence_scale: high = stated on an nps.gov/recreation.gov page fetched for this file; medium = secondary source or older official page; low = inferred or general knowledge, verify before shipping
meta.staleness_rule: Any condition claim dated before 2025-01-01 is flagged stale:true.

meta.fact_check: Fact-checked 2026-10-08 against nps.gov area pages, NPS trail and road conditions, Recreation.gov division text, USFS alerts and WSDOT. See design/data/FACT_CHECK.md.

permits.summary: Every overnight stay in the ONP wilderness needs a wilderness camping permit, year-round. Reservations are first-come, first-served on Recreation.gov (permit 4098362); there is no early-access lottery. Summer-season quota inventory is bulk-released April 15 at 7:00 AM Pacific and is not topped up later.

required_for.value: All overnight stays in undeveloped (backcountry) areas, year-round. Day hikes need no wilderness permit (park entrance fee/pass still applies).

system.value: Recreation.gov permit #4098362 (Olympic National Park Wilderness Permits). You pick an entry trailhead, then a camp area for each night. Once WIC staff issue the permit (about 3 days before the start), you log in and print it yourself.

lottery.value: None. ONP has no early-access lottery (unlike Mount Rainier); all reservations first-come, first-served.
lottery.note: Confirmed 2026-10-08: the Recreation.gov permitcontent API for permit 4098362 returns has_lottery=false and lotteries=null (record modified 2026-09-30). The NPS reservations page (2026-02-12) describes only first-come-first-served booking.

high_elevation_note.value: High-elevation camps are typically reservable mid-July to mid-October only. Earlier or later high trips must be arranged by phoning the WIC. Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin quota season is narrower than May 15-Oct 15 and depends on snow.

walk_ups.value: No camp sites are held for same-day walk-ups. Some inventory shows 'In Station' on Recreation.gov and can only be booked by contacting the WIC.

fees_2026.annual_pass_note: Covers nightly fees (not the $6 reservation fee) for 12 months from purchase month.

park_entrance_fees.value: Separate from wilderness fees, collected at entrance stations (e.g. Heart O' the Hills/Hurricane Ridge, Elwha, Sol Duc, Hoh, Staircase).

value.area: Ozette Coast (Yellow Banks to Point of the Arches)
value.notes: Includes Cape Alava and Sand Point camps. Shi Shi Beach (north of Point of the Arches) is outside the quota zone but still needs a permit and a Makah Recreation Pass.

No camping within 0.25 mi of Scout Lake; camp only at marked sites. Fact check 2026-10-08 additions: Quota area with designated sites only, max 6 per regular site plus a group site, no campfires, and two composting toilets. Recreation.gov: 7.3 mi and about 3,850 ft from the trailhead. No camping within 0.25 mi of Scout Lake. The Lena Creek ford about 0.5 mi below the lake can be hazardous. NOTE: no region file models this trail yet (fact check 2026-10-08).

value.area: East Fork Quinault River / Enchanted Valley
value.notes: Trial quota since May 15, 2024, up to 3 years: max 208 users or 30 permits per night, whichever first. Final decision not found as of 2026-10. Fact check 2026-10-08: the NPS reservations page (updated 2026-02-12) still describes the trial: 208 users or 30 permits per night, with public comment accepted May 15-Oct 15 during the trial. 2026 is therefore the third and probably final trial season. The 2024 WTA figure of 12 permits/night is not supported by any NPS page.
CLOSED 2025-2026 by Bear Gulch Fire (see current_conditions).

NPS scope (reservations page 2026-02-12): Deer Park to Obstruction Point (Roaring Winds camp), Obstruction Point to Grand Pass, Badger Valley and Lake Lillian. Designated sites at Grand, Moose and Gladys lakes. No campfires in Grand Valley.

value.area: Sol Duc / Seven Lakes Basin / Mink Lake area (including Cat Basin, High Divide, Little Divide)
Hoh River Trail - Elk Lake, Martin Creek, and Glacier Meadows camps are quota sites; Hoh River group and stock sites are quota sites

rules_in_quota_areas: Camp only in designated sites (red camps on the Trip Planner map).
No deviation from the permit itinerary except in an emergency.
Groups of 7-12 must reserve group sites in all quota areas.
Quota inventory is bulk-released; no later release.
quota_areas.non_quota: Brown camps on the Trip Planner map: permits not limited, but a permit (and fee) is still required.

group_size.large_group: 7-12 people; must use designated group sites in Sol Duc/Seven Lakes Basin, Hoh Lake Trail, Hoh River Trail, Grand Valley, Upper Lena Lake and Lake Constance (and all quota areas per reservations page). Many camps can only take 1-6.
group_size.affiliated_groups: May not combine above 12; must camp and travel at least 1 mile apart.

cancellation_and_changes.value: Cancel 3+ days before start: camping fee refunded, $6 kept. Within 3 days or no-show: no refund. Party size/camp changes allowed (if space) until the day before or until issued; after issuance only a WIC ranger can change it.

port_angeles_wic.location: Olympic National Park Visitor Center, 3002 Mount Angeles Road, Port Angeles, WA 98362
port_angeles_wic.hours: Daily 9 AM - 5 PM, year-round; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas
port_angeles_wic.role: Issues permits for the whole park; handles advance reservations for quota areas; loans bear canisters during business hours.

quinault_wic.location: Quinault Rain Forest Ranger Station, 913 North Shore Road, Amanda Park, WA 98526
quinault_wic.normal_season: Memorial Day weekend through end of September
quinault_wic.status_2026: CLOSED for the 2026 season (trail conditions page, Sept 2026). Year-round bear canister return bin. Confirmed by the WIC page updated 2026-09-29 ('Current Hours: Closed').

other_ranger_stations_for_game.value: Historically seasonal WICs/ranger stations also operated at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center, Staircase Ranger Station, Kalaloch, Ozette and Sol Duc; in 2026 nps.gov lists only Port Angeles (year-round) and Quinault (seasonal, closed 2026) as WICs. Game can show other stations as 'ranger station - info only'.

trip_planner_map.value: The NPS Wilderness Trip Planner / Wilderness Trail & Campsite map color-codes camps: red/yellow = quota (designated sites, reservation needed), brown = non-quota. It also marks toilets.

national_forest_note.value: Trailheads on Olympic National Forest land (e.g. Lena Lake, Lake Constance approach via Dosewallips Road, Royal Basin via Dungeness trailhead, Upper Quinault) may require a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass for parking; forest rules differ (e.g. dogs allowed on forest trails, no permit for forest camps outside the park).

food_storage.summary: As of 2026, approved hard-sided Animal Resistant Food Containers (ARFC, 'bear cans') are required in ALL wilderness areas of the park, including the entire wilderness coast. Hanging food and bear wires no longer count as compliant. All food, garbage and scented items stay in the can 24 hours a day except while being carried, prepared or eaten.

rule.value: ARFCs required in all wilderness areas. Front-country alternatives: hard-sided vehicle or park food locker. Fact check 2026-10-08: confirmed. The NPS food storage page (2026-07-07) says canisters are 'required in all wilderness areas of the park', and all 156 publicly listed Recreation.gov camp areas repeat the requirement, including coast, valley, lake and high camps. This settles the PNT Association's 'most' wording: the rule is park-wide.
rule.page_dates: food storage page updated 2026-07-07; regulations page updated 2026-03-30; trail conditions updated 2026-09-30

history.value: Before the 2026 park-wide rule, canisters were required only in certain zones (High Divide/Seven Lakes Basin, the wilderness coast, Enchanted Valley after 2015 bear closures, Grand Valley/Royal Basin and several lake camps) and food could be hung (12 ft up, 10 ft out from trunk) or put on bear wires elsewhere. The Pacific Northwest Trail Association describes the 2026 change as 'most wilderness areas'; NPS pages say 'all'. Game should follow NPS: canister everywhere overnight.
history.older_hanging_standard: 12 ft high and 10 ft from the nearest trunk (2009 NPS release) - historical only

hanging_and_wires.value: PROHIBITED, not merely non-compliant. Every publicly listed Recreation.gov camp area for the park (156 of 156 non-hidden camp divisions; division text current to 2026-09-30) says: 'Hanging food, garbage or scented items, whether on a bear wire system or self-constructed bear hang, is prohibited.' Older bear wires still physically exist at some camps (e.g. Elwha, Hoh, Quinault valleys) but may not be used. (Fact check 2026-10-08.)

approved_containers_2026.note: Model list is from the NPS approved list (updated 2026-06-25). Unlisted containers are not permitted regardless of maker claims; damaged/cracked cans not allowed. Volumes/weights are manufacturer or retailer specs gathered for this file (not on the NPS page); null = not verified.

items.model: BV110b, BV200, BV250, BV300, BV350, BV400 (older models)

items.note: Retailers list 600-615 cu in; weight ~2.7 lb from general knowledge

stock_panniers: Bear Country Camping SFO and HFO
Outfitters Supply TrailMax Bear Proof Pack Panniers
Steel salvage drum with security lid (e.g. 8-gal open head)

loaner_program.value: Free loaner canisters for permit holders at the Port Angeles WIC (and Quinault when open) during business hours; not reservable; can run out on busy weekends. Local outfitters also rent.

game_capacity_rule_of_thumb.value: BearVault rates its 11.5 L BV500 at up to ~7 days of food for one person and its 7.2 L BV450 at 3-4 days, i.e. very roughly 1.5-1.7 L of canister per person-day for typical backpacking food (dense, repackaged). Bulky or fresh food fills it faster. Two people on a 4-night trip typically need two cans or one large can plus very careful packing - a natural pack-fitting puzzle for the game.

small_animal_problems.value: Rodents (mice, chipmunks, ground squirrels, marmots), gray jays, ravens and on the coast raccoons are the most frequent food thieves. Raccoons on the wilderness coast are notorious for opening packs and soft containers. Royal Basin had rodent problems reported in June 2026. Mountain goats and deer seek salt from urine and sweaty gear. Food loss and chewed gear are realistic minor consequences.

examples.report: raccoons take food from unattended packs/tents; canisters required on the entire coast

bear_incidents_context.value: Enchanted Valley was closed to camping in 2015 after bears obtained food and became habituated; reopened with canisters required. A possibly habituated bear was reported near Boulder Creek camp (Elwha) in 2026.

elevation_limit.value: Campfires and wood-burning camp stoves allowed only below 3,500 ft. Gas/canister stoves allowed everywhere unless a ban says otherwise.

value: Wilderness coast between the headland at Wedding Rocks and the headland north of Yellow Banks (Ozette area, includes Sand Point) - no fires or wood stoves
Olympic Hot Springs and Boulder Creek Campground - year-round burn ban

Hoh River Trail at and above Elk Lake, including Glacier Meadows and the Blue Glacier moraine. NPS trail conditions (2026-06-14) say 'at or above Elk Lake'. The NPS Hoh River Trail page and the 2024 restrictions notice say 'above Martin Creek' (from 1/4 mi north of Elk Lake). Recreation.gov still allows fires at Martin Creek camp itself.
Lake Angeles and Heather Park camps (above 3,500 ft)
Mt. Storm King (day use only, no fires)
All high camps above 3,500 ft (Seven Lakes Basin, High Divide, Royal Basin, Grand Valley, etc.)
Royal Basin: all camps, including Royal Creek. The NPS Royal Basin page (2026-01-28) says 'No campfires in Royal Basin'; Recreation.gov's Royal Creek text conflicts.
Grand Valley: Grand, Moose and Gladys lakes (NPS Grand Valley page, 2026-01-21: 'No campfires in Grand Valley').
Appleton Pass / Oyster Lake and Hoh Lake (NPS trail pages).
Low Divide (3,600 ft): above the 3,500-ft limit per the NPS North Fork Quinault page, although Recreation.gov's Low Divide text says fires are permitted. Treat it as no-fire.

coast_rules.value: Where fires are allowed on the coast, use driftwood below the high tide line, small fires, never against drift logs (log fires can burn for days and drift logs can roll); no fires Wedding Rocks to north of Yellow Banks.
coast_rules.note: Driftwood/below-high-tide guidance is long-standing NPS coast guidance; the Wedding Rocks-Yellow Banks ban is high confidence.

seasonal_bans.value: Park-wide campfire restrictions are imposed in dry late summers (e.g. Sept 2012, summer 2015 Paradise Fire year, 2021 heat wave, 2023, 2024 - lifted Sept 2024) and in 2025 during the Bear Gulch Fire. Typical window: July-September. Game: roll a seasonal fire ban in Aug-Sep with some probability.

attendance.value: Campers must stay with a campfire from start to finish and extinguish it fully.

pets.value: Not allowed on park trails, meadows, beaches or undeveloped areas. Exceptions: leashed pets on Rialto Beach north to Ellen Creek and on the Kalaloch beach strip between the Hoh and Quinault reservations (no camping with pets there), and the Spruce Railroad Trail. Pets are allowed on adjacent Olympic National Forest trails.

stock.value: Only horses, mules, burros and llamas. Max 12 people/8 stock. Above 3,500 ft stock must camp only in designated stock camps and stay on maintained trails. Pellets or rolled grain only (no loose hay/viable seed). Tie 200+ ft from water using hitch rails or highlines, not trees. Grazing within 1/4 mi of stock camps, move every 12 h. Many trails closed to stock (nature trails, most coast; Hoh River Trail beyond Martin Creek stock camp except llamas).

drones.value: Launching, landing or operating unmanned aircraft anywhere on park lands or waters is prohibited.

bicycles_wheels.value: No bicycles or wheeled devices on park trails except the Spruce Railroad Trail; bikes may be used on closed roads (e.g. washed-out Olympic Hot Springs Road to the Boulder Creek trailhead).

weapons.value: Weapons other than legally carried firearms are prohibited on trails/undeveloped areas; discharging firearms is prohibited. (Page phrasing on firearms is inconsistent; follow federal law: possession per state law, discharge prohibited.)

fishing.value: No state license required inside the park; park fishing regulations apply. Elwha River and tributaries closed to fishing.

leave_no_trace_and_waste.status_of_lnt: LNT principles are guidance, not regulation, except where codified (food storage, fires, designated sites in quota areas, waste rules).

human_waste.value: Use backcountry toilets (privies/vault/composting toilets) where present. If more than 1/4 mile from a privy, dig a cathole 6-8 inches deep at least 200 ft (about 70 steps) from water, trails and camps; pack out toilet paper. Urinate on rocks or trail tread so deer and goats do not dig up plants for salt.

toilets.value: Toilets are marked on the Wilderness Trail & Campsite map; NPS has installed self-contained vault toilets at the busiest backcountry areas (e.g. Seven Lakes Basin, where full waste containers are flown out). Staffing limits mean seats may not be cleaned regularly. Lake Constance: south vault toilet closed, north composting toilet open (June 2026).

mount_olympus_and_glaciers.value: Blue bags (pack-out waste bags) are REQUIRED on Mount Olympus. They are available at the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center and the Port Angeles WIC (NPS Climbing Mount Olympus page, updated 2026-01-21). No waste may be left on the lateral moraine. Climbers' camps are only at Caltech Rocks and Snow Dome; camping between Glacier Meadows and the Blue Glacier is not allowed. Pit toilets on the approach: 5-Mile Island, Olympus Guard Station, Lewis Meadow, Elk Lake and Glacier Meadows.

coast.value: Toilets at the main camp concentrations at Cape Alava and Sand Point and at other high-use beach camps; elsewhere dig a cathole 6-8 in deep, 200 ft from camps and water. Camp above the high-tide line. Fires only on open beach, below the high-tide line and at least 10 ft from drift logs, using beach driftwood only; no fires from north of Yellow Banks to the headland at Wedding Rocks. No camping between the Quillayute River and Ellen Creek (Rialto Beach day-use strip); on the Kalaloch strip south of the Hoh River camping only in frontcountry campgrounds. Treat water: iodine does not kill Cryptosporidium; some creeks are brackish near high tide. Beware rolling drift logs in surf and washed-up metal canisters (report, do not touch). Fact check 2026-10-08, privy list from the NPS route pages: North Coast (page updated 2026-08-24) has pit toilets at Ellen Creek, Cedar Creek, Norwegian Memorial, Chilean Memorial, South Sand Point, Sand Point, Cape Alava, both sides of the Ozette River and Shi Shi Beach. South Coast (2026-08-19) has privies at Third Beach, Toleak Point and Mosquito Creek; Scott Creek has none at present. Seafield Creek's maximum group size is 6. Wedding Rocks, Sand Point and South Sand Point water sources usually dry up late in summer.

camping_placement.value: In quota areas camp only at designated sites. Elsewhere use established sites ('good campsites are found, not made'). Upper Lena Lake: no camping within 0.25 mi of Scout Lake. General LNT: camp and wash 200 ft from lakes/streams.

washing.value: Carry water 200 ft from lakes and streams; use tiny amounts of biodegradable soap; scatter strained gray water.

water_treatment.value: Treat all water: filter or boil. Chemical treatments are not effective against Cryptosporidium (park guidance).

climate.summary: Olympic has a marine climate with a very wet season (Oct-Apr) and a short, fairly dry summer (Jul-Aug). The west side (coast, Hoh, Queets, Quinault, Bogachiel) gets ~100-170 in of precipitation a year; the northeast rain shadow (Port Angeles, Sequim, Dungeness/Gray Wolf, Royal Basin) gets far less (Port Angeles ~26 in). High country above ~4,500 ft is normally snowbound from November to June; Hurricane Ridge averages roughly 30-35 ft of snowfall a year. July-September is the backpacking season for high routes.

nps_statements.value: Coast and west-facing valleys get 100-170 in/yr; Port Angeles 25-30 in; Hurricane Ridge 30-35 ft snow/yr; high trails may be impassable from snow into June (later in big years); snow can return to the high country as early as late September; by late October rain and wind reach the valleys and beaches. Summer thunderstorms in high country; summer coastal fog.
nps_statements.extra: NPS: sea-level summer days usually 60-70 F; high-mountain winter lows seldom below 0 F; fog often forms after sunset and lingers to late morning (fog drip adds 30+ in of moisture to coastal forest).

coast.proxy_station: Quillayute Airport (UIL), 180 ft, 3 mi inland from La Push - NOAA 1991-2020 normals
coast.notes: Beach itself is a few degrees cooler in summer (fog, onshore wind). Summer fog is common mornings. Snow at sea level is rare (Quillayute ~13 in/yr in 1966-2005 record, usually melts in a day).

rain_forest_valleys.proxy_station: Clearwater (Queets valley edge, ~250 ft) - NOAA 1991-2020 normals. The Hoh Rain Forest is wetter (~135 in/yr per NPS).

hoh_rain_forest_annual_precip_in.alt: NPS text says 'almost 12 feet' (~144 in); seasonal table shows 135.0 in/yr at the Hoh vs 103.0 at Kalaloch, 25.9 Port Angeles, 15.8 Sequim

rain_forest_valleys.upper_valley_note: Up-valley camps (e.g. Hoh: Olympus Guard Station ~950 ft, Elk Lake ~2,550 ft) are wetter and a few degrees cooler; lapse ~3-3.5 F per 1,000 ft.

rain_shadow_lowlands_and_north_valleys.notes: Inland valleys (Elwha) are warmer by day in summer (mid-70s F) and colder at night in winter than the coast.

waterhole_snotel.location: Obstruction Point Road near Waterhole, ~3 mi from Obstruction Point (Grand Valley/Badger Valley country)

buckinghorse_snotel.location: Upper Elwha interior near Hayes River/Dodger Point country - wetter interior subalpine

dungeness_snotel.location: Upper Dungeness (rain shadow; Royal Basin approach)

subalpine_4000_6000ft.notes: Computed for this file from NRCS SNOTEL daily data (means of daily max/min; precipitation from daily accumulations). SNOTEL temperatures sit in clearings and can read a little warm on sunny days. Exposed ridges and passes (High Divide 5,100-5,400 ft, Grand Pass 6,450 ft) are windier and colder. Summer nights at Seven Lakes Basin/Royal Basin/Grand Valley commonly 35-45 F; frost possible any month, likely by mid-September.

alpine_glacier_6000ft_plus.value: No long-term weather station on Mount Olympus (a station at 6,910 ft near the Blue Glacier ran 1957-1963). Estimate from Waterhole (5,010 ft) with a lapse of ~3.5 F per 1,000 ft: Glacier Meadows (~4,200 ft) similar to Waterhole; Blue Glacier/Snow Dome (6,500-7,000 ft) July-Aug highs ~55-58 F, lows ~38-40 F on fair days; summit (7,980 ft) July-Aug highs ~50 F, lows near freezing. Storms bring sub-freezing temps, wind and whiteout any month. NPS estimates over 50 ft of snow a year on Mount Olympus; published precipitation estimates range ~180-250 in/yr. Park glacier area shrank 46% from 1982 to 2015; Blue Glacier has retreated over 1/3 mile since 1919.

freezing_level_ft.method: Computed for this file from 1991-2020 00Z/12Z Quillayute (UIL) radiosonde soundings (NOAA IGRA2, station USM00072797): lowest height where air temperature crosses 0 C, by month. These are free-air values over the coast; snow level in precipitation is typically ~1,000 ft below the freezing level. Low percentiles include cold clear mornings where the surface itself is at or below freezing.
freezing_level_ft.game_use: Roll a daily freezing level from the month's distribution (e.g. normal or triangular fit to p10/median/p90), shift down 2,000-4,000 ft on storm days. If camp elevation > freezing level - 1,000 ft and it is precipitating, it snows.

snow_free_dates.method: Computed for this file from NRCS SNOTEL daily snow-water-equivalent: melt-out = first day after Mar 1 with zero SWE for 3 days running.

recent.2026: May 11 (low snowpack: peak SWE 18.8 in vs ~44 in median)

dungeness_3990ft.note: Rain-shadow site melts ~7-8 weeks earlier than Waterhole.

trail_rule_of_thumb.value: Lowland/valley trails below ~2,500 ft are mostly snow-free year-round except brief storms. 3,500-4,500 ft: snow-free roughly late May-mid June. Open subalpine benches 4,500-5,200 ft (Grand Valley, Royal Lake, Seven Lakes Basin floor): typically late June-early July. North-facing slopes, passes and gullies above 5,000 ft (High Divide between Heart Lake and Bogachiel Peak, Hoh Lake-Bogachiel, Appleton Pass, Grand Pass, Royal Basin upper, Anderson Pass, Low Divide, Lake Constance outlet, Glacier Meadows/avalanche chute) hold steep snow until mid-to-late July in a normal year and into August in big years; NPS reserves high camps mid-July to mid-October for this reason. Ice axe/traction useful for snowfields early season.

first_autumn_snow.value: First lasting snow (>=1 in SWE) at Waterhole: median about Nov 1; at Buckinghorse about Oct 25; earliest Sept 30 (2013). Light dustings above 5,000 ft can come any time after mid-September.

rivers.pattern: Two high-water seasons. (1) Rain floods Oct/Nov-Feb from atmospheric rivers ('Pineapple Express'): rivers can rise 5-10x in a day (e.g. Hoh went ~2,600 to >27,000 cfs in under 24 h in Dec 2024). (2) Snowmelt high water May-early July on rivers fed by high country (Elwha, Dungeness, Hoh, Quinault), worst in late afternoon/evening on warm days and lowest in early morning. Lowest, easiest fords: late July-September. Autumn rains usually return in early-mid October.
rivers.ford_notes: Queets River ford at the trailhead is generally only possible below ~800 cfs (NPS), i.e. typically August-September, and still waist-deep. Other named fords that become dangerous in rain or snowmelt: Hoh River Trail fords before Olympus Guard Station, North Fork Sol Duc at 1 mi, Ozette River (coast), Goodman/Falls/Mosquito creeks (south coast), Cameron Creek, White Creek (East Fork Quinault), Elip and Wild Rose creeks and the Quinault near Sixteen Mile (North Fork), Big Creek (Quinault), Upper Duckabush, Lena Creek, Nine Stream (N Fork Skokomish), Elwha south of Chicago Camp, Calawah and Bogachiel (Snider-Jackson).

daylight_48N.location: computed for 47.95 N, 123.6 W (central park), sea-level horizon, 15th of each month, Pacific time with DST
daylight_48N.notes: Deep valleys lose 1-2 h of direct sun at each end of the day. Daylight in October is ~5 h shorter than in late June - a real planning constraint for long days.

storms_and_seasons.summer: July-August is the driest window (Quillayute ~9 rain days/month vs ~22 in winter). Afternoon thunderstorms occasionally hit the high country; marine fog on the coast; heat waves (e.g. late June 2021) can push valleys above 90 F and accelerate snowmelt.
storms_and_seasons.first_autumn_storms: The first significant Pacific frontal system usually arrives late September to mid-October (Quillayute precipitation jumps from ~4.6 in in September to ~10.7 in in October). Historic big autumn windstorms: Columbus Day Storm (Oct 12, 1962). Atmospheric rivers cluster Oct-Feb.
storms_and_seasons.winter: Nov-Mar: 20+ precip days/month on the west side; snow level often 1,500-4,000 ft; high country under 5-15 ft of snow; Hurricane Ridge winter-only weekend access.
storms_and_seasons.spring: Apr-Jun: still wet; snowmelt raises rivers; avalanches on steep slopes into June; high trails snowbound.

tides.summary: The Olympic coast has mixed, mainly semidiurnal tides: usually two highs and two lows per day of unequal height (a 'higher high' and 'lower high', a 'higher low' and 'lower low'), with roughly 6 h 12 min between successive high and low and each day's pattern ~50 min later than the day before. Occasionally only one low or one high falls on a calendar day. Heights are referenced to MLLW (0.0 ft = mean lower low water), so a 'minus tide' is lower than average.

reference_station.name: La Push, Quillayute River, WA
reference_station.nps_recommends: NPS tells coastal hikers to use NOAA predictions for station 9442396.

neah_bay_for_comparison.note: Neah Bay (9443090) near Shi Shi has similar timing, ~0.5 ft smaller range.

constituents_la_push.note: Top harmonic constituents (amplitude ft, Greenwich phase deg, speed deg/hr) from NOAA. Form factor (K1+O1)/(M2+S2) = 0.58 -> mixed, mainly semidiurnal.

observed_2026_statistics.method: From NOAA 2026 high/low predictions at La Push (MLLW, local time).
observed_2026_statistics.timing_pattern: Spring-summer: the lowest (minus) tides fall in early-mid morning (05:00-10:00). Autumn-winter: the lowest tides fall in the evening (17:00-21:00), often after dark. Hence daylight low-tide windows are scarcest Sept-Oct.
observed_2026_statistics.spring_neap: Biggest ranges and minus tides come every ~14.8 days around new and full moon (spring tides); smaller ranges near quarter moons (neap tides), when some low-tide-only points may stay closed for several days.

rules: Carry a current tide table (La Push 9442396) and a coast map that marks headlands as passable below a stated tide height, 'round at low tide', 'caution' or impassable (Custom Correct and NPS maps).
A point labeled 'passable below X ft' can be rounded only while the predicted tide is below X ft MLLW; plan to round it within 1-2 hours before low tide, on a falling tide, never on a rising tide.

Some headlands are never passable on the beach - use the overland trail, marked by round red-and-black targets, often with ropes, cable ladders or wooden ladders (ropes are not NPS-maintained; test them).
Storm surge, swell and strong onshore wind raise water above predictions, especially Oct-Apr; add margin.
Creek mouths (Goodman, Falls, Mosquito, Cedar, Ozette River, etc.) are deeper at high tide and after rain - cross at low tide.
Camp above the high-tide line and beware floating/rolling drift logs in surf.

named_examples_ft.note: Point-by-point details belong in the coast region file. Examples from NPS route pages: South Coast - Diamond Rock passable below ~2 ft (can stay closed for days); between Scott Creek and Strawberry Point ~4 ft; ~3 mi south of Third Beach ~4.5 ft; Scott's Bluff north-side washout passable on beach only below 1 ft (2026). North Coast from Rialto - 2.4 mi N ~5 ft; Cape Johnson (4.3 mi N) ~4 ft; 5.1 mi N ~5.5 ft; 7.9 mi S of Ozette TH ~6 ft; several 4-6 ft points between Point of the Arches and Seafield Creek.

game_simulation.recommended: Sum of cosines with the La Push constituents above: h(t) = 4.58 + sum_i A_i * cos(speed_i * t_hours + phase_i). Use M2, S2, N2, K1, O1, P1 at minimum; this yields realistic unequal semidiurnal tides, a spring-neap cycle (~14.8 d) and occasional single-low days. For a storybook game the absolute astronomical phase need not match the real calendar: pick a random epoch per trip (or anchor t=0 to the in-game date's moon phase) and keep it consistent across the trip so the printed in-game tide table matches what happens.
game_simulation.storm_surge: Add +0.5 to +2 ft on storm days (more in winter) and hide it from the printed table - the player only learns it via the narrator ('the sea is running higher than your tide card promised').
game_simulation.point_check: For each tidal point: passable on beach if h(t) < limit_ft (+ margin for surf); else take overland trail (if one exists: slower, slip risk, rope events) or wait. Being caught between two closed points on a rising tide = classic 'cliffed out' scenario (in gentle mode: you wait, cold and wet, until the tide drops).
game_simulation.printed_table_format: Show 'TIDES - LA PUSH' with date, time (h:mm am/pm) and height to 0.1 ft for each H/L, as hikers see on NPS/Recreation.gov printouts.

search_and_rescue.summary: ONP typically handles about 50-60 search-and-rescue incidents a year (71 by early September 2019). Most are ground efforts for slips, trips and falls that leave someone unable to walk out (especially lower-leg injuries), overdue or lost parties, and hypothermia from cold rain; a smaller number involve river crossings, falls from cliffs/waterfalls, coastal tide strandings and climbing accidents on Mount Olympus. Helicopter support comes from Naval Air Station Whidbey Island, Coast Guard Air Station Port Angeles, and contract short-haul helicopters (e.g. from Mount Rainier). Cell coverage is absent in most of the backcountry.

patterns.description: Ankle/leg injuries far from roads; patients carried or flown out. E.g. Labor Day 2019: hiker with ankle injury at Lake La Crosse walked 8 mi to Home Sweet Home for short-haul helicopter.

The classic Olympic killer is not deep cold but 35-50 F rain with wind, wet cotton, and a party that keeps going or gets lost. Lost/disoriented hikers found hypothermic; Mount Olympus climbers benighted without gear. Early-season and autumn high-country trips, and the coast in winter storms, are highest risk.

Overdue parties are reported by family; navigation errors on primitive routes (Bailey Range, Skyline, Six Ridge, snow-covered High Divide), off-trail descents into drainages. Example: Sept 2021, a solo backpacker on an Enchanted Valley-Marmot Lake-Six Ridge loop was reported overdue after ~8 days and hoisted from the Seven Stream drainage ravine, found by his flashlight, with minor injuries.

Swift, cold, glacier- or rain-fed rivers. Aug 2001: a hiker drowned fording the rain-swollen East Fork Quinault about 0.5 mi below Enchanted Valley Chalet where a bridge had washed out. Fords are worst during afternoon snowmelt (May-July) and autumn rain.

Sol Duc Falls: Sept 2019 a 15-year-old went over the falls (~40-50 ft) and survived via technical rope rescue; June 2025 an 18-year-old died after crossing the upper river and falling over the falls during hot-weather snowmelt flows.

Hikers stranded on rocks or cliffs by rising tide and hoisted by Coast Guard (Third Beach 2018, four hikers; Jefferson Cove/Hoh Head 2021, two hikers climbed a cliff to escape the tide and were hoisted at 2 a.m.; Shi Shi 2014). Injuries from falls on headland trails (Toleak Point 2016) and drift logs rolled by surf.

Mount Olympus (7,980 ft) via Hoh River Trail, Glacier Meadows, Blue Glacier, Snow Dome, Crystal Pass and summit block: crevasse falls (1993 fatal fall into crevasse after unroping on the Blue Glacier), falls from the summit block (2013 fatal), benightment and hypothermia, Glacier Meadows avalanche-chute ladder. NPS treats it as a technical climb (glacier travel, crevasse rescue gear).

Early-season steep snow on passes and gullies (High Divide, Heather Park, Hayden Pass) and winter/spring avalanche chutes; Feb 2026 two hikers fell in an avalanche chute on Mount Ellinor (Olympic National Forest) and were helicopter-rescued.

Rare. One fatal attack in park history: mountain goat, 2010. Cougar attacks on children: Lake Angeles 2023-07-29 (8-year-old, minor injuries), Hurricane Ridge near Victoria Overlook 2025-07-20 (4-year-old, flown to Harborview; collared cougar killed next morning). Black bear problems are about food, not attacks.

rescue_resources.value: Call 911 (park dispatch). Little or no cell service in valleys and most high country; texts sometimes get through from ridges. Satellite messengers/PLBs are the reliable option. Helicopter hoists: NAS Whidbey Island SAR (MH-60), USCG Air Station Port Angeles (MH-65), contract short-haul from Mount Rainier; ground teams include Olympic Mountain Rescue and county SAR. Weather often grounds aircraft for days.

nps_safety_advice: Leave a trip plan and emergency plan
Stay behind viewpoint fences; do not cross above waterfalls

game_design_mapping.note: Incident types above map directly to game hazards. Suggested base per-day probabilities for a WELL-prepared party in good weather are low (well under 1%); multiply by risk factors: missing rain gear/insulation (x5 hypothermia in rain), cotton clothing (x3), no map/compass on primitive routes (x5 lost), fording at peak snowmelt afternoon or in rain (x5-10), coast without tide table (x10 stranding), early-season high route without traction (x5 slip), overdue beyond itinerary (rescue triggered). Numbers are design suggestions, not statistics.

general_rules.value: Stay at least 50 yards from all wildlife (park regulation; the same page also says 75 ft for medium-large animals); if an animal reacts to you, you are too close. Never feed, bait or call wildlife. Report bears that come within 50 yards, enter camp or try for food; report all cougar sightings; report any mountain goat sighting anywhere on the peninsula; report aggressive elk.

black_bear.value: Only black bears live in the park (no grizzlies). Problems are food-conditioning: Enchanted Valley closed to camping Apr-Jun 2015 after bears got human food (Pyrites Creek to O'Neil Pass junction); 'large bear population' noted there in 2026; possibly habituated bear at Boulder Creek camp 2026. Encounter: make noise, give space, stand your ground and look big, never run; secure food in canister 24 h; cook away from tents. Bears graze meadows (High Divide, Seven Lakes Basin, Enchanted Valley, Hoh) especially July-Sept huckleberry season.

cougar.value: The whole park is cougar habitat. Do not hike alone; keep children close and in sight; leave pets home. Encounter: do not run, group together, appear large, keep eyes on it, make noise and shout, throw rocks; if attacked fight back. Incidents: Lake Angeles 2023-07-29 (child, closure of Lake Angeles/Heather Park/Klahhane Ridge/Switchback trails), Hurricane Ridge 2025-07-20 (child, collared cougar killed). Report: (360) 565-3000 or 911.

mountain_goat.value: Non-native (about 12 released near Lake Crescent 1925-1929). Robert Boardman (63) was fatally gored on the Switchback Trail/Klahhane Ridge on 2010-10-16 - the only fatal wildlife attack in park history; the goat was shot. Goats sought human salt (urine, sweat). Removal: ~725 goats in 2018; 2018-2020 aerial captures translocated 325 to the Cascades; fall 2020 ground teams removed 31; 2021-2022 aerial lethal removal 192; active phase ended Aug 2022 with 548 removed. Maintenance phase since 2023; only 5 sightings (1 confirmed) 2023-2025. Game: goats are now essentially a historical/rare sighting; the salt-seeking lesson still applies to deer and marmots (urinate on rock away from trails).

roosevelt_elk.value: NPS calls elk one of the most dangerous animals in the park. Give extra room during the fall rut (roughly Sept-Oct) and spring calving (roughly late May-June). Common in Hoh, Queets, Quinault, Bogachiel valleys and on the coast near Kalaloch.

small_animals.value: Deer, marmots, chipmunks, mice, gray jays and ravens raid unattended food and chew packs, boots and trekking-pole grips for salt; raccoons are a well-known problem on the coast. Small animals near camp can draw predators and carry disease. All solved by canister + clean camp.

marine.value: Do not approach or try to rescue stranded marine mammals on beaches; report them. Watch for gray whales (spring/fall migration), sea otters, harbor seals, bald eagles.

current_conditions.as_of: 2026-10-04 (NPS Alerts & Conditions page); trail details from NPS trail conditions page updated 2026-09-30; road page updated 2026-08-07

staircase_bear_gulch_fire.value: Bear Gulch Fire (2025) closed Staircase-area trails. As of 2026-09-30 still CLOSED: North Fork Skokomish (Staircase to First Divide), Four Stream, Wagonwheel Lake, Flapjack Lakes, Gladys Divide, Black and White Lakes primitive, Smith Lake, Home Sweet Home, Six Ridge (Mt. Olson junction to N Fork). Reopened: Staircase Rapids Loop; Six Ridge Lake Sundown to Belview Camp. Six Ridge Primitive closed since 2025-08-01.

elwha.value: Olympic Hot Springs Road washed out; vehicles stop at Madison Falls parking; adds ~6.5 mi to Whiskey Bend TH and ~8 mi to Boulder Creek TH (bikes allowed on road, not past trailhead). Elwha River Trail cleared to Hayes River Camp; 45 trees down Hayes River to Chicago Camp; landslide undercutting 20 ft section ~0.5 mi south of Hayes River junction; ford south of Chicago Camp (no log). Fire-damaged sections (2023 Delabarre/Elwha-area fires).

hoh.value: Hoh River Trail: two fords before Olympus Guard Station (low on 2026-06-01, impassable in moderate/heavy rain); 37 downed trees TH to Glacier Meadows; avalanche-chute ladder (below Glacier Meadows) has 3 broken and 1 missing rungs; 5 Mile Island stock hitch washed away; no fires at/above Elk Lake. Hoh Lake trail cleared (2026-08-17), no water until C.B. Flats.

bogachiel.value: Washout before Mosquito Creek (steep bypass); Bogachiel Camp sites eroded into river; washout between Flapjack and 15 Mile camps.

sol_duc_high_divide.value: Sol Duc River trail minimal blowdown; High Divide and Lunch Lake had patchy steep snow Heart Lake-Lunch Lake (mid-June 2026); North Fork Sol Duc ford at 1 mi 3-4 ft deep (2026-06-02).

hurricane_ridge_area.value: Royal Basin snow-free to Royal Lake (2026-06-05), rodents, no self-pay parking box. Lower Gray Wolf washout - upper Gray Wolf/Slab Camp not reachable from Lower Gray Wolf TH. Heather Park steep snow, washouts. Little River slide 0.5 mi past first foot-log.

dosewallips.value: Dosewallips Road washed out east of the (former) campground - adds 6.5 mi of road walking. West Fork snow-free to Anderson Pass with several fords; Main Fork 19 + 21 trees down to Hayden Pass; Hayden Pass eroded/exposed west side.

queets.value: Queets River ford at trailhead dangerous; more likely fordable below ~800 cfs (Hwy 101 gauge), still waist-deep; generally not fordable late fall-spring. 29 trees down to Bob Creek; washout 0.3 mi west of Bob Creek; camping past Bob Creek not recommended (2015 Paradise Fire).

quinault.value: South Shore Road washout (outside park) - Graves Creek and North Fork reached only via North Shore Road. Quinault WIC closed for 2026. North Fork: Stalding Creek bridge damaged/closed (ford). East Fork: washout ~1/3 mi before Enchanted Valley; White Creek ford; large bear population in Enchanted Valley. Big Creek: no bridge.

coast.value: South Coast: large washout north side of Scott's Bluff - beach passage only below 1 ft tide. Ozette River ford required on Shi Shi-Cape Alava, may be impossible in winter or at high tide. Headland ropes not NPS-maintained. Cannonball Island (Tskawahyah) closed (Makah/Ozette reservation).

duckabush_lena.value: Duckabush: 50+ trees down to Upper Duckabush ford; ford hazardous/impassable winter, early summer and after rain. Upper Lena Lake open, Lena Creek ford hazardous at times.

roads.note: Road status changes often. Every entry carries the date of the claim. Game can treat these as 'fall 2026' defaults and roll seasonal/random closures on top.

road_weather_line.date: 2026-08-07 (NPS Current Road Conditions page: "Call (360) 565-3131 for recorded road and weather information updated daily")

items.road: US 101 Hoh River Bridge (south of Forks; WSDOT)
items.status: Single-lane alternating traffic, signals and 25 mph since 2026-07-14 (cracked floor beams). FULL CLOSURES to all traffic: 5 am Sept 24 - 5 pm Sept 29, 5 am Oct 1 - noon Oct 6, and 5 am Oct 8 - noon Oct 13, 2026, after nightly closures Sept 14-22. The emergency repair project runs to Sept 2028, so more closures are possible.
items.impact: No other crossing of the Hoh exists near the coast. During full closures the Forks / Rialto / La Push / Hoh Rain Forest side is cut off from Kalaloch, Ruby Beach, Queets and Quinault, and the detour around Hood Canal takes 4+ hours. Oil City Road and the Upper Hoh Road turn off north of the bridge, so they stay reachable from Forks.

items.road: Hurricane Ridge Road (Port Angeles - Heart O' the Hills - Hurricane Ridge, 17 mi)
items.status: OPEN to the ridge; Hurricane Hill Road open
items.seasonal_pattern: Summer: open daily, may close for weather. Winter (late Nov - end Mar): Fridays-Sundays and holiday Mondays only, weather permitting, all vehicles must carry chains (2025-26 schedule; 2024-25 hours were 9 AM-4 PM, cars out by 5 PM). Mar 31 - Apr 30: may open/close depending on conditions.
items.work_2026: Water system and utility replacement in Hurricane Ridge developed area; asphalt patching and striping may cause rolling closures.
items.services: Intermittent staffing, limited services, NO potable water on Hurricane Ridge (2026). No overnight camping in lots.

items.status: DESTROYED by fire May 7, 2023; demolished fall 2023. Temporary restroom trailers and a visitor contact station (installed 2023) remain the only facilities: no food, rentals, indoor warming space or drinking water.
items.replacement: Pre-design (architect: Anderson Hallas Architects); ~$80M secured in 2024 disaster supplemental; design/RFP expected 2027, construction possibly from 2028.

items.road: Obstruction Point Road (gravel, ~7.8-8 mi from Hurricane Ridge)
items.status: OPEN (opened 2026-06-17)
items.seasonal_pattern: Typically mid-July to mid-October; snow drifts often delay opening; not suitable for RVs, trailers or buses. Closed rest of 2022 season; closed during 2023 fires.

items.road: Deer Park Road (gravel, steep, from US-101 east of Port Angeles)
items.status: OPEN (opened 2026-06-09); not suitable for RVs or trailers
items.seasonal_pattern: Typically opens early-mid June, closes mid-October (weather). Upper road snowbound in winter.

items.status: CLOSED TO VEHICLES at Madison Falls parking area due to washout (since 2015 floods; continuously closed since at least 2021). Open to pedestrians, bicycles, stock and leashed pets. Adds ~6.5 mi to Whiskey Bend TH and ~8 mi to Boulder Creek (Appleton Pass/Hot Springs) TH.
items.long_term: NPS studied relocating ~1 mi of road near Sanders Creek out of the floodplain (2018-2019 FONSI for geotech, ~$8.3M estimate); no 2025-2026 construction decision found.
items.date: road page entry 2021-05-07, reconfirmed on conditions page 2026-10-04

items.status: OPEN (reopened 2026-03-24 after winter closure)
items.seasonal_pattern: Often closed or gated in winter (snow to ~2,000 ft; Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort closed in winter). Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort, RV park and campground open summer 2026.

items.status: OPEN
items.history: Washout at MP 9.7 in Dec 2024 flood (Hoh River rose from ~2,600 to >27,000 cfs in under a day); reopened 2025-05-08 with state emergency funds. Brief Aug 2025 closure from culvert work flooding. 2026 repairs at MP 0.3 and 0.8 with one-way traffic and up to 20-min delays late May-Aug 2026. A second atmospheric-river flood on 2025-12-10 damaged the road near MP 10 and closed it from the entrance station for about four weeks (NPS spokesperson via press; reopening planned for early January 2026). The road was open again in 2026 (NPS road page entry 5/5/26). Added by fact check 2026-10-08.
items.visitor_center: Hoh Rain Forest VC open daily 9 AM-4:30 PM (2026); entrance waits up to 2 hours in summer - arrive before 8 AM or after 5 PM.

items.status: OPEN; not recommended for RVs/trailers; subject to closure on short notice for hazardous weather
OPEN; the only access to Graves Creek and North Fork trailheads
PARTIAL CLOSURE: washout ~8 mi from US-101 (Jefferson County, outside park)

items.status: OPEN since 2026-05-28; RVs and trailers prohibited. Was closed spring 2026 (erosion at mile 4.1; reported 2026-04-23). History: 2023 Pony Bridge/road bridge repairs.
OPEN; narrow gravel, not recommended for RVs/trailers

CLOSED TO VEHICLES at washout (Olympic National Forest land) ~6.5 mi before the old Dosewallips campground/ranger station; hikers walk the old road. Washout dates to 2002; USFS rebuild project shown 'Cancelled' (page updated 2025-09-18). Feb 2026 trip report: Pass Creek bridge on the road walk ~0.7 mi past the decommissioned ranger station collapsed.
items.date: road page entry 2017-08-25; USFS 2025-09-18; trip report 2026-02-14

items.status: OPEN since 2026-07-08 after a 12-month closure for the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire. Developed area, campground, ranger station and Staircase Rapids Loop open; ALL wilderness trails beyond the developed area remain closed (as of 2026-09-30). FS-2451 and Copper Creek Trail (national forest) closed.
Hoko-Ozette Road OPEN; SR 112 has had frequent closures/detours from flooding and landslides - check WSDOT. Ozette primitive campground open but often closes in winter for flooding.

CLOSED beyond Mora Campground to vehicles, bikes and pedestrians July 8 - Oct 15, 2026 for permanent repair of 2019 flood damage near MP 1.25. Rialto Beach (south trailhead of the North Coast route) not reachable by road until it reopens. Mora Campground open.
items.date: 2026-07-08 to 2026-10-15 (some press said Oct 5; NPS says Oct 15)

items.status: Area open; Kalaloch ranger station closed; Kalaloch Campground reservations May 15-Sep 20, 2026; South Beach CG first-come May 19-Oct 10, 2026.
Lake Crescent Lodge open; Fairholme Campground, Fairholme Store and Log Cabin Resort closed; Storm King Ranger Station closed for season.
Intermittent construction Apr 29 - Oct 2026 (2021 atmospheric-river damage repairs).

bear_gulch_fire_2025.value: Human-caused; started 2025-07-06 near Mount Rose (Olympic National Forest) above Lake Cushman; ~20,232 acres; 100% contained Nov 2025 (USFS says 2025-11-12). Closed Staircase area for a year; wilderness trails in N Fork Skokomish drainage still closed 2026-09-30 for hazard assessment and bridge/privy repair.

fires_2026.value: Mount Tom Creek Fire (lightning, near Mount Olympus, Hoh drainage) burning from June 2026; Lake of the Gods camp closed (June). Aug 2026: Mt. Barnes Fire (0.5 ac, reported Aug 14, ~1.5 mi SE of Mt. Barnes summit), Maiden 2 fire (0.7 ac, near Maiden Peak, extinguished), small tree fire near Deer Park CG (extinguished). No closures as of 2026-08-26.

campfire_ban_2026.value: Stage 2 fire restrictions from 2026-08-07: ALL campfires prohibited in Olympic NP and Olympic NF (including charcoal); gas/propane stoves OK if 3+ ft from flammable vegetation. Still in effect 2026-08-26; no lifting notice found as of 2026-10-07 (autumn rains usually lift bans mid/late September). Fact check 2026-10-08: the Olympic National Forest Stage 2 order ran from Aug 7, 2026 12:01 am through Oct 1, 2026 (unless rescinded earlier). On 2026-10-08 the Olympic NF alerts page no longer listed any fire restriction and showed fire danger 'Moderate'. NPS had posted no rescission notice that this check could find; the NPS fire page (updated 2026-09-18) and alerts page (2026-10-04) list no ban. Treat the ban as probably expired on national forest land after Oct 1. Its status inside the park is unconfirmed, so default to the normal rules (fires below 3,500 ft in existing rings, none in listed no-fire areas) and have a ranger or WIC check confirm.

fires_2023.value: Lightning on 2023-08-28 started several fires: Delabarre (~4,165 ac, upper Elwha) and Low Divide (~340 ac, N Fork Quinault) were largest; closures included Elwha River Trail to Low Divide, Hayden Pass, Dosewallips, N Fork Quinault, Skyline, Martins Park, Obstruction Point Road. Most reopened 2024. Burned sections still produce blowdown and hazard trees (2026 reports).

fires.older_fires_still_visible: Paradise Fire 2015 (Queets valley above Bob Creek), Hayes Fire 2016 (Hayden Pass blowdown), 1978 burn on Hoh Lake trail.

enchanted_valley_chalet.value: Historic 1930s chalet moved ~100 ft back from the eroding East Fork Quinault in Sept 2014; by Mar 2019 the bank was again ~5 ft away; 2020 EA recommended dismantling/removal; as of 2025-2026 reporting no final decision or action - the building still stands on its moving beams, closed to entry. Treat as a landmark, not shelter.

rule_flavor_for_planning_phase: Permit desk: player must choose a trailhead and a camp for every night; quota camps (Seven Lakes Basin, High Divide, Royal Lake, Grand Valley, Hoh Lake, Glacier Meadows, Elk Lake, Lake Constance, Upper Lena, Enchanted Valley, Ozette coast) can be 'full' on summer weekends; itinerary must be followed in quota zones.
Fee calculation: $8 per adult per night + $6 per permit; youth 15 and under free; optional $45 annual wilderness pass. Plus park entrance $30/vehicle (or annual pass).
Bear canister is mandatory for any overnight trip (loaner available at Port Angeles WIC but can run out on busy weekends) - canister volume caps food days and is a natural pack-fitting puzzle.
Season gate: high camps only reservable mid-July to mid-October; outside that window or in a big-snow year, steep snow and ice on passes.
Coast trips need a tide table printout and map; points have 'passable below X ft' limits.
Fire rules: no fires above 3,500 ft or on the Ozette coast; seasonal bans Aug-Sep (2026 had a Stage 2 total campfire ban from Aug 7) - packing a stove matters.
No dogs on park trails; no drones; group max 12.

closed_or_altered: Staircase wilderness trails closed (Bear Gulch Fire): Flapjack Lakes, N Fork Skokomish, Wagonwheel, Black and White Lakes, Home Sweet Home, Four Stream, Gladys Divide
Elwha road walk from Madison Falls (+6.5 mi to Whiskey Bend, +8 mi to Boulder Creek)
Rialto Beach unreachable by road until Oct 15, 2026
South Shore Quinault Road washout (use North Shore)
Hurricane Ridge: no lodge, no potable water
Lake of the Gods camp closed in June 2026 (Mount Tom Creek Fire) - current status unknown
fall_2026_scenario_defaults.permit_season: Summer season ends Oct 15; from Oct 16 winter season rules apply (no quota at most high camps but snow likely).

game_design_notes.worst_case_tone_support: Real incident patterns (sprained ankle 8 miles from a helipad, a hypothermic night, a ford that should not have been tried, a tide that cut off a headland) give ready-made gentle 'ranger rescue / trip ends early' outcomes, and harsher optional-mode outcomes, without inventing implausible hazards.
